## LaporCovid-19

Scores draw on two peer-reviewed articles [@ekawati2022; @rinaldi2024] and the
coalition's own report [@laporcovid2021]. A civil-society coalition of public
health experts, scientists, journalists and activists, which describes itself as
a citizens' coalition, founded the initiative [@ekawati2022; @laporcovid2021].
The coalition designed the reporting platform, ran the database with volunteers,
analysed and published the data, and advocated for families of health workers,
so every Domain A stage was scored as led (`Y`) and the case is classed as
extreme citizen science. It counted health-worker deaths while no official
figure was published (C1 and C2 = `Y`). Its contribution to policy on
compensation is self-reported (C3 = `P`). The organisation continued after the
emergency phase as LaporSehat and LaporIklim, but the status of the health-worker
death database is not documented (D1 = `P`; rescored from `NR` after a follow-up
search on 16 November 2026, see S1.5 and S3). Under the verdict rules in S1.4,
C3 = `P` and D1 = `P` give the verdict partial.

Leadership note: leading roles were held by civil-society experts, journalists and activists; lay members of the public mainly reported data.
